cornell.name: Cornell University
cornell.blurb: The most transfer-friendly Ivy — but rates have tightened fast in recent cycles. See what changed.
overview: Cornell admits transfer students at a noticeably higher rate than its single-digit first-year admit rate, but that gap has been closing. Recent cycles have swung between roughly 9% and 14%, with about 670–830 students admitted each year out of applicant pools ranging from 6,500 to 7,200.

Cornell currently accepts transfer applicants for fall entry only — spring transfer has been paused in recent cycles, so applicants should plan around the fall pathway. Decisions are released on a rolling basis rather than all at once, typically starting in late April and continuing into June.
lookingFor: At least 12 completed semester credit hours in college coursework at the time of application
Strong, consistent grades in college-level coursework — competitive applicants are well above Cornell's minimums

Coursework that aligns with the specific college and major within Cornell the applicant is targeting (requirements vary meaningfully by school — Engineering, AAP, and Human Ecology all have distinct prerequisites)
A College Report and Mid-Term Report from the applicant's current institution confirming academic and disciplinary standing
A compelling personal statement explaining why transferring to Cornell specifically supports the applicant's academic goals
requirements: Common Application for Transfer, with Cornell's college-specific supplement, due March 15 for fall entry
Official transcripts from every college attended, plus a final high school transcript
College Report and Mid-Term Report completed by an official at the applicant's current school
Program-specific materials where required — e.g., a portfolio for Architecture, Art, and Planning applicants, or a design challenge for some Human Ecology applicants
Decisions released on a rolling basis from late April through June

mentor.text: Full Axis has two mentors who transferred into Cornell. Andrew Wei and Kellen Bell both work directly with Cornell-bound applicants on building a college-specific strategy, since requirements shift dramatically between Cornell's schools.

cornell.dataNote: Acceptance rates and deadlines shift year to year and can vary by college within Cornell. Figures above reflect recent published cycles as a general guide — confirm current numbers on Cornell's official admissions site before finalizing your application strategy.

uc-berkeley.name: UC Berkeley
uc-berkeley.blurb: Nearly double the freshman admit rate, dominated by California community college applicants.
overview: UC Berkeley admits roughly a quarter of its transfer applicant pool most years, which is meaningfully higher than its single-digit first-year acceptance rate. Recent cycles have hovered in the 24–27% range, with Berkeley extending offers to somewhere between 4,000 and 5,500 transfer students annually out of applicant pools in the 19,000–21,500 range. The overwhelming majority of admits — over 90% in recent years — come from California community colleges, reflecting the UC system's priority on the community college transfer pathway.

Berkeley only accepts transfer applicants for fall entry, and does not use letters of recommendation or official transcripts during initial review — the personal insight questions and reported coursework carry the weight.
lookingFor: Completion of all lower-division prerequisite coursework for the intended major before enrolling — major preparation matters more here than at most schools
A strong GPA in UC-transferable coursework, with competitive applicants often well above the stated 3.0 minimum
Completion of the required English composition and quantitative reasoning coursework
Compelling responses to the required major-readiness essay plus a set of personal insight questions
requirements: University of California application, opening August 1 and due by November 30 for fall entry
Minimum 60 UC-transferable semester units (90 quarter units) completed by the end of spring term prior to enrollment
Transfer Academic Update (TAU) submitted by January 31, reporting fall grades and planned spring coursework
Decisions typically arrive in mid-to-late April, released directly through the applicant's UC portal

mentor.text: Full Axis has a UC transfer mentor. Alec Sarkissian transferred from Sacramento City College into UC Berkeley's College of Letters and Science and was admitted to every UC campus he applied to — he works directly with UC-bound applicants on TAG strategy and course planning.

uc-berkeley.dataNote: Acceptance rates and deadlines shift year to year. Figures above reflect recent published cycles as a general guide — confirm current numbers on UC Berkeley's official admissions site before finalizing your application strategy.

vanderbilt.name: Vanderbilt University
vanderbilt.blurb: A rare elite private school where transferring can be a smarter path in than first-year admission.
overview: Vanderbilt's freshman acceptance rate has fallen into the low single digits, but its transfer pathway remains far more accessible — recent cycles have landed in the high-teens to low-20s, with roughly 550–700 students admitted out of applicant pools between 2,900 and 3,200.

Vanderbilt only offers a fall transfer option. Applicants are strongly encouraged to meet the February 15 priority deadline, though the university continues reviewing applications on a rolling basis until May 1. Decisions go out on a rolling basis too, beginning in late April, so there's no single notification date for every applicant.
lookingFor: At least 12 completed semester credit hours, with strong and consistent academic performance
A clear, specific reason for transferring — Vanderbilt places real weight on why the applicant believes Vanderbilt (and their intended school within it) is the right next step
Demonstrated engagement outside the classroom, not just a strong transcript
For Peabody College applicants, a declared major and fit for that specific program; for Blair School of Music, a required audition
requirements: Coalition Application for Transfer or Common Application for Transfer, with the February 15 priority deadline (rolling review continues through May 1)
Final high school transcript, including date of graduation
Official transcripts from every college attended
One letter of recommendation, ideally from a college instructor
Program-specific materials where required — an audition for Blair School of Music, a stated major for Peabody College

mentor.text: Full Axis has a mentor with direct Vanderbilt admissions experience. Azmain Harun, admitted to Vanderbilt, works with applicants on positioning their transfer narrative and choosing the right school within the university.

vanderbilt.dataNote: Acceptance rates and deadlines shift year to year. Figures above reflect recent published cycles as a general guide — confirm current numbers on Vanderbilt's official admissions site before finalizing your application strategy.

boston-university.name: Boston University
boston-university.blurb: One of the most transfer-friendly major research universities, with two intake cycles per year.
overview: Boston University is one of the more transfer-friendly major research universities in the country. Recent cycles have put the transfer acceptance rate roughly in the high-20s to mid-30s — well above BU's freshman acceptance rate, which has fallen into the single digits for Regular Decision. BU typically admits somewhere in the 2,000–2,300 range out of applicant pools of 4,500–6,700.

Unlike most highly selective schools, BU accepts transfers for both fall and spring entry, though not every major or college is open to spring admission. Fall carries the larger intake and more program options. Decisions are released on a rolling basis, generally between April and June for fall applicants.
lookingFor: At least 12 completed college credits (12+ credit applicants apply as transfers; fewer, and the first-year path applies instead)
A strong, consistent college GPA — the single most heavily weighted factor, with admitted students often at 3.5 or higher
A declared major within one of BU's degree-granting schools or colleges — transfer applicants cannot apply undeclared
Fit with the specific program applied to — Questrom School of Business, the College of Engineering, and Sargent College tend to be the most competitive for transfers
requirements: Common Application (Transfer version), due February 1 for fall entry or October 1 for spring entry
Official transcripts from every college attended, plus a high school transcript if fewer than 30 college credits are completed
One letter of recommendation from a college instructor familiar with the applicant's work
No SAT/ACT scores required for transfer admission
Decisions released on a rolling basis, generally April through June for fall applicants

mentor.text: Full Axis works with BU-bound applicants on program selection and application strategy, since acceptance odds vary significantly between BU's schools and colleges.

boston-university.dataNote: Acceptance rates and deadlines shift year to year and vary by school within BU. Figures above reflect recent published cycles as a general guide — confirm current numbers on Boston University's official admissions site before finalizing your application strategy.

harvard.name: Harvard College
harvard.blurb: One of the most selective transfer programs in the country, admitting only a very small number of students each year.
overview: Harvard College maintains one of the nation's smallest and most selective transfer programs. In recent admission cycles, the university has typically admitted between 10 and 20 transfer students from applicant pools of roughly 1,300 to 1,600, resulting in an admit rate around 1%.

Harvard accepts transfer applications for fall enrollment only. Applicants submit materials by March 1, and admissions decisions are generally released in mid- to late May. Because so few students are admitted, successful applicants usually demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, a compelling reason to transfer, and a strong record of impact beyond the classroom.
lookingFor: Outstanding academic performance in a rigorous college curriculum, typically with grades near the top of the applicant's class
Evidence that transferring to Harvard is essential for the applicant's academic and intellectual goals, rather than simply seeking a more prestigious institution
Strong engagement outside the classroom through leadership, research, service, entrepreneurship, or other meaningful contributions
Positive academic and disciplinary standing at the current institution, supported by the required College Report
Thoughtful application essays that clearly explain the applicant's educational journey, reasons for transferring, and fit with Harvard's academic community
requirements: Common Application for Transfer, including Harvard's transfer supplement, due March 1
Official transcripts from all colleges attended, along with a final high school transcript
College Report completed by the applicant's current institution and an Academic Evaluation from college instructors
Standardized test scores are optional under Harvard's current testing policy, though applicants should verify the policy for their application year
Admission decisions released in mid- to late May for fall enrollment

stanford.blurb: Stanford enrolls only a handful of transfer students each year, making it one of the country's most selective transfer destinations.
overview: Stanford's transfer admission process is among the most competitive in higher education. In recent years, the university has admitted roughly 30 to 60 transfer students from applicant pools exceeding 2,000 applicants, with admit rates typically around 1–2%.

Transfer applicants may apply only for fall enrollment. Admissions decisions are generally released in mid-May, and successful applicants demonstrate exceptional college achievement, significant personal impact, and a compelling academic reason for transferring.
lookingFor: Outstanding academic performance in a rigorous college curriculum
Evidence of exceptional intellectual curiosity, initiative, and meaningful contributions outside the classroom
A clear explanation of why Stanford uniquely supports the applicant's academic and personal goals
Strong faculty recommendations that speak to college-level achievement
Continued academic and disciplinary good standing at the current institution
requirements: Common Application for Transfer due March 15
Official transcripts from every college attended and final high school transcript
College Report and instructor evaluations
Transfer essays explaining academic interests and reasons for transferring
Admission decisions released in mid-May

caltech.name: California Institute of Technology
caltech.blurb: One of the smallest, most STEM-intensive transfer programs in the country — a handful of seats each year.
overview: Caltech's transfer program is tiny even by elite-school standards. Recent cycles have seen anywhere from roughly 150 to 180 transfer applicants, with single-digit-percentage admit rates that have ranged from under 2% to around 6% depending on the year — a reflection of how few seats open up in a school with fewer than 1,000 undergraduates total.

Transfer applicants may apply for fall entry only. Applications are due February 1, and decisions are released by mid-April, with admitted students given until June 1 to decide. Applicants for the 2025–26 cycle onward are required to submit SAT or ACT scores, reversing Caltech's earlier test-optional policy.
lookingFor: Exceptional preparation in mathematics, physics, and other core STEM coursework, evaluated against Caltech's core curriculum
Outstanding grades in a rigorous college course load, with little to no room for weak marks in technical subjects
Completion of the required Entrance Examinations in mathematics and physics as part of the transfer process
A genuine, specific reason for wanting Caltech's small, intensely research-focused environment rather than a larger STEM program
Meaningful research, engineering, or independent project experience outside the classroom
requirements: Common Application or QuestBridge Application, due February 1 for fall entry
Official transcripts from every college attended, plus a final high school transcript
Caltech Transfer Entrance Examinations in mathematics and physics, proctored under Caltech's policies
SAT or ACT scores required for the 2025–26 application cycle and beyond
Decisions released by mid-April, with a June 1 reply deadline

northwestern.name: Northwestern University
northwestern.blurb: A large, transfer-friendly research university that recently added an Early Decision option for transfers.
overview: Northwestern admits transfer students at a noticeably higher rate than its ultra-selective freshman pool, with recent cycles generally landing between 12% and 17%. For fall 2024, the university received just over 4,000 transfer applications and admitted roughly 12% of them.

Starting with the 2025–26 cycle, Northwestern introduced a binding Early Decision option for transfers — due March 2, about a month before the April 1 Regular Decision deadline — following the same move by the University of Chicago the year before. Northwestern only admits transfers for the fall term, and it does not require SAT or ACT scores.
lookingFor: At least one full year of college coursework completed (24 semester credit hours) by the time of enrollment
Strong, consistent grades in a range of liberal arts and science coursework, not just a narrow major-specific track
A clear sense of purpose and academic direction — Northwestern wants to see genuine intent behind the choice of school and major, not an 'undecided' placeholder
Meaningful engagement outside the classroom that shows how the applicant will contribute to campus life
For Bienen School of Music applicants, a required audition; theatre program space is limited and only occasionally open to transfers
requirements: Coalition Application or Common Application for Transfer, due March 2 for Early Decision or April 1 for Regular Decision
Official transcripts from every college attended, plus a final high school transcript
Transfer Writing Supplement, with an additional personal statement recommended
No SAT/ACT scores required under Northwestern's test-optional transfer policy
Decisions released on a rolling basis, with a guaranteed response by the end of May

uchicago.name: University of Chicago
uchicago.blurb: A distinctive Transfer Early Decision option sits alongside UChicago's more traditional rolling transfer review.
overview: UChicago's transfer acceptance rate has fluctuated in recent cycles, generally landing in the mid-single digits to around 9%. For fall 2024, the university received roughly 2,900 transfer applications and admitted about 9.3% of them; the year before, 1,821 applicants saw a 7.9% admit rate.

The university offers a unique Transfer Early Decision (TED) plan — a binding commitment similar to first-year ED — due March 1, alongside Transfer Rolling Decision for applicants who want to keep other options open. Both plans share the same priority deadline, though Rolling Decision applications are technically accepted through June 1. UChicago only admits transfers for fall entry.
lookingFor: Strong, consistent grades in a rigorous college course load — competitive applicants often present GPAs well above 3.5
Thoughtful, specific essays that explain why the applicant is leaving their current institution and how UChicago's academic environment fits their goals
Intellectual curiosity and comfort with UChicago's discussion-driven, rigorous academic culture
For TED applicants, a genuine, first-choice-level commitment to UChicago, since the plan is binding
Optional supplemental materials (research, creative work, portfolios) for applicants with relevant talents or experience
requirements: UChicago's transfer application, with Transfer Early Decision or Transfer Rolling Decision options, priority due March 1
Official transcripts from every college attended, plus a final high school transcript
College/transfer report and two instructor evaluations
One extended essay of the applicant's choice plus a short 'why UChicago' essay
Rolling Decision applications accepted through June 1; decisions typically follow within several weeks of a complete file

jhu.name: Johns Hopkins University

Hopkins accepts transfer applicants for fall entry only, into the entering sophomore or junior class. Applicants must have completed more than 12 semester credits at another institution. Decisions are generally released in mid-May.

dartmouth.name: Dartmouth College
